data.why: EPICC bundles three ready-to-run YAML cost models (measles, measles_oregon, tb_isolation); the measles.yaml is also a valid file to exercise the 'Load Custom Model > Upload File' dialog since it is schema-identical to a user-authored model.

goals: Select a bundled epidemiological model and review its default cost assumptions and sources before running it
Adjust cost and epidemiological parameters (hospitalization cost, wages, contact rates, vaccination coverage) to match a local setting
Run the simulation and compare cost breakdowns (medical, productivity, contact tracing) across outbreak-size scenarios
Share a specific parameterized calculation with a colleague via a URL that encodes the current inputs
Load or author a custom cost model (via YAML upload, URL, or pasted model code) to analyze a different disease or setting
Export the results as a PDF or DOCX report for stakeholders

review.summary: The tree captures EPICC's purpose and its stated workflow well: choose a model and read its sourced assumptions, set local parameters and presets, run across scenarios, share by URL, files and report, and load or author models. Most cited screens match their nodes. It should not be filed until the inverted preset-precedence claim and two mis-cited screens are fixed, the parameter-file reload round trip and a report-export feature are added, and the three unreplayed tasks are checked again.
